persona.who: 23, just quit a Zomato job to build a D2C brand with a friend. No funding yet. Parents think it's a phase but are supportive.
persona.note: quit my job last week to go all in on our brand. no money yet but honestly ive never felt more alive. i want to stay like this and not lose this fire when it gets hard

understanding.emotion: alive and afraid of losing it
understanding.bridge: What you are living with is what the texts call starting what is yours to build, and that is where this week begins.

week_beats.hook: You recognise the resolve as yours, and the fear of losing it as real.

understanding.core_struggle: A young person who just quit their job to build a brand from nothing feels more alive than ever and wants to keep that fire when the hard days come.
understanding.mirror: You left the job that paid, and now you are building something that pays with life instead.
understanding.insight: Nothing is wrong with you, and nothing needs fixing. The resolve is real and it is your own now. What will test it is the morning the work stops being exciting.
understanding.mechanism_label: Starting what is yours to build

queries.hook: A fire lit by the choice to build something of your own; the resolve to stay alive in it, not just successful.
queries.diagnose: Resolve fades when the mind runs ahead to the prize or looks sideways at others; it holds when the work itself is the reward.
queries.steady: No honest effort on the right path is ever wasted; even a little of it protects you and carries you forward.
queries.act: Rise and act; do your work fully and well each day, let the result go, and keep at it when no one is watching.
queries.story: A young warrior who set out to build something from nothing, faced the first setback, and kept their resolve through it.

understanding.seat: a young person who just left a job to build a brand from nothing
understanding.life_context: Under twenty-five and building something of their own; they left a job last week to go all in on a brand that has no money yet, and they are riding a high they have never felt before.
details: started a brand with no money
wants to keep the fire when it gets hard

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna on duties by nature and finding fulfilment in your own work.
verse.sanskrit: श्रेयान्स्वधर्मो विगुणः परधर्मात्स्वनुष्ठितात् । स्वभावनियतं कर्म कुर्वन्नाप्नोति किल्बिषम् ॥
verse.line: Better your own path, imperfectly walked, than someone else's done perfectly.
verse.translation: Better is one's own duty, though imperfect, than the duty of another well performed. Doing the work born of one's own nature, one incurs no wrong.
verse.why: Do the work that fits you, flaws and all, as an offering.
verse.misuse: Not 'stick to the role you were born into'. It's about honest fit with your own nature, not caste or family script.

prasang.title: Duties by nature, and their fruit
prasang.summary: After listing duties by varna, Krishna says one reaches perfection through one's own work done as worship, and that one's own path, though imperfect, beats another's, since every undertaking has flaws.
prasang.lesson: Do the work that fits you, flaws and all, as an offering.

verse.meaning: Arjuna stands on a battlefield, confused about which path to take. Krishna tells him that the right path is the one that comes from your own nature. It is better to walk your own path, even if you stumble, than to walk someone else's path perfectly. You do not carry a sin for doing the work that fits you.
verse.for_you: You quit your job last week because the work felt like air. That is your own nature speaking, and it is worth more than a perfect salary. Let the brand be a sketch. Do your own work, even when it is rough, and trust that the fire you feel is the right kind of heat.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on working in the world without being stained by it.
verse.sanskrit: युक्तः कर्मफलं त्यक्त्वा शान्तिमाप्नोति नैष्ठिकीम् । अयुक्तः कामकारेण फले सक्तो निबध्यते ॥
verse.line: Let go of the payoff and you find lasting peace. Chase it and it chains you.
verse.translation: The disciplined person, giving up the fruit of action, attains lasting peace. The undisciplined, attached to the fruit and driven by desire, is bound.
verse.why: Be in the mess without letting it soak in.
verse.misuse: Letting go of the payoff isn't refusing fair pay or recognition; it's not being chained to it.

prasang.title: Marks of the knower and the doer
prasang.summary: The disciplined person acts without attachment, like a lotus leaf untouched by water, and finds peace by letting go of the fruit.
prasang.lesson: Be in the mess without letting it soak in.

verse.meaning: Krishna speaks to Arjuna about how to act in the world. He says that a disciplined person finds lasting peace by giving up the payoff of their actions. The undisciplined person, driven by desire for results, becomes bound. It is about acting without letting the outcome stain your mind.
verse.for_you: You want to keep the fire when it gets hard. That means you cannot hold the brand's success in your hands every morning. Do the work because it is yours, and let the payoff sit on the other side of the field.

verse.speaker: Bhartrihari
verse.sanskrit: निन्दन्तु नीतिनिपुणा यदि वा स्तुवन्तु लक्ष्मीः समाविशतु गच्छतु वा यथेष्टम् । अद्यैव वा मरणमस्तु युगान्तरे वा न्याय्यात्पथः प्रविचलन्ति पदं न धीराः ॥
verse.line: Let them praise or blame, let money come or go: the steady don't step off the right path.
verse.translation: Let the worldly-wise blame or praise; let fortune come or go as she pleases; let death come today or ages hence: the steadfast do not move a step from the path of what is right.
verse.why: Setbacks rarely last for those who keep going on the right path.

prasang.title: Nitishatakam: On steadfastness
prasang.summary: Steadfastness: the gods kept churning the ocean past jewels and poison until they found nectar; the steady do not leave the right path whatever people say. A struck ball bounces back and a cut tree grows again.
prasang.lesson: Setbacks rarely last for those who keep going on the right path.

verse.meaning: Bhartrihari is speaking to the reader about what it means to stay true. He says let the worldly-wise blame or praise. Let fortune come or go as she pleases. Let death come today or ages hence: the steadfast do not move a step from the path of what is right. The idea is that your work has its own rhythm. Setbacks rarely last for those who keep going on the right path.
verse.for_you: You are building your own brand with no money, and the high is real. The path is yours now. The test will come when praise turns to blame, or when the money does not. Stay on the path.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on how to act without being chained to results.
verse.sanskrit: नेहाभिक्रमनाशोऽस्ति प्रत्यवायो न विद्यते । स्वल्पमप्यस्य धर्मस्य त्रायते महतो भयात् ॥
verse.line: No sincere effort here is ever wasted. Even a little of it shields you from great fear.
verse.translation: On this path no effort is lost and no harm results. Even a little of this practice protects one from great fear.
verse.why: Do the work fully; let go of owning the result.

prasang.title: The yoga of action
prasang.summary: Krishna teaches the yoga of action: work wholeheartedly, give up clinging to outcomes, stay even in success and failure, and keep a single steady purpose.
prasang.lesson: Do the work fully; let go of owning the result.

verse.meaning: Krishna is telling Arjuna about the yoga of action. He says no sincere effort here is ever wasted. Even a little of it shields you from great fear. The point is to do the work fully and let go of owning the result. Work wholeheartedly, give up clinging to outcomes, and keep a single steady purpose.
verse.for_you: You cannot control if the brand takes off. You can only control the work itself. Do it fully today, and let the result be what it will be.

verse.speaker: Vidura
verse.setting: Vidura counsels the sleepless King Dhritarashtra the night before the peace talks.
verse.sanskrit: निश्चित्य यः प्रक्रमते नान्तर्वसति कर्मणः / अवन्ध्यकालो वश्यात्मा स वै पण्डित उच्यते
verse.line: Decide, then begin. Don't stall halfway, don't waste time, and keep yourself steady.
verse.translation: One who begins only after deciding, does not stop halfway through the work, does not waste time and keeps himself in hand, is called wise.
verse.why: Decide calmly, act steadily, forgive freely, and know what real happiness is made of.

prasang.title: Vidura Niti: the wise and the fool
prasang.summary: Sleepless before the peace talks, King Dhritarashtra calls his half-brother Vidura for counsel. Vidura describes the marks of the wise and the fool, the faults that block progress, and the six joys of life.
prasang.lesson: Decide calmly, act steadily, forgive freely, and know what real happiness is made of.

verse.meaning: The night before the great peace talks, the sleepless King Dhritarashtra calls for his wise half-brother Vidura. Vidura tells him that a wise person decides calmly, then begins, does not stop halfway, does not waste time, and keeps themselves steady. That is the mark of wisdom. What comes next in the story is that the king ignores this counsel and the war begins anyway.
verse.for_you: The work you started last week is the decision made. Today, give your full attention to the next small task. Do not look ahead to the hard days or the money. Just steady your hand on what is in front of you now.

verse.speaker: Vidura
verse.setting: Vidura counsels the sleepless King Dhritarashtra the night before the peace talks.
verse.sanskrit: करिष्यन्न प्रभाषेत कृतान्येव तु दर्शयेत् / धर्मकामार्थकार्याणि तथा मन्त्रो न भिद्यते
verse.line: Don't announce your plans; let people see your results.
verse.translation: Don't talk about what you are going to do; let people see only what you have done. That way your plans for duty, pleasure and gain are never exposed.
verse.why: Let results speak before announcements do.

prasang.title: Vidura Niti: trust, secrecy and quarrels
prasang.summary: Vidura speaks of welcoming guests, keeping plans private until done, whom to trust, and how quarrels with the powerful end.
prasang.lesson: Let results speak before announcements do.

verse.meaning: Still in that same counsel, Vidura tells King Dhritarashtra that a wise person does not announce their plans. They let people see only what has been done. That way, their intentions for duty, pleasure, and gain remain hidden and safe. The story shows that announcing too much brings quarrels and exposes you to those who might use your words against you.
verse.for_you: Keep the details of your new brand to yourself for now. Let your first small results do the talking instead of your plans. Let the work show before you explain it.

story.title: Hanuman's leap
story.story_hook: Halfway across the ocean, a golden mountain rose out of the water and offered him a place to rest.
story.summary: Hanuman leaps across the ocean. A mountain rises to repay an old kindness by offering rest; he thanks it but keeps his promise not to stop. He outwits Surasa by shrinking small and defeats Simhika, and the watching beings praise his steadiness, sight, judgement and skill.
story.lesson: Gratitude and focus can go together; know when to be big and when to be small.

anchor.speaker: Beings of the sky
anchor.setting: Having outwitted two monsters mid-flight, Hanuman is praised by those watching from the sky.
anchor.sanskrit: यस्य त्वेतानि चत्वारि वानरेन्द्र यथा तव। धृतिर्दृष्टिर्मतिर्दाक्ष्य स कर्मसु न सीदति ॥
anchor.line: Steadiness, clear sight, good judgement and skill. With these four, you won't sink at work.
anchor.translation: Whoever has these four, as you do, chief of monkeys, never sinks in his work: steadiness, clear sight, judgement and skill.
anchor.why: Gratitude and focus can go together; know when to be big and when to be small.

prasang.title: Hanuman's leap
prasang.summary: Hanuman leaps across the ocean. A mountain rises to repay an old kindness by offering rest; he thanks it but keeps his promise not to stop. He outwits Surasa by shrinking small and defeats Simhika, and the watching beings praise his steadiness, sight, judgement and skill.
prasang.story_hook: Halfway across the ocean, a golden mountain rose out of the water and offered him a place to rest.
prasang.lesson: Gratitude and focus can go together; know when to be big and when to be small.

story.hook_title: Halfway across the ocean, a mountain rose up and offered Hanuman a rest
story.teaser: Halfway across the ocean, a mountain rose up and offered Hanuman a rest
story.for_you: Hanuman kept his promise to the mountain and his focus on the goal. They are building something from nothing. The fire they feel will test them when the work becomes ordinary. Let your steadiness, your clear sight, your good judgement and your skill carry you across the ocean.

script: You are riding a high that you have never felt before. You left a job last week to build something of your own. Everything is changing at once, and you want to keep the fire when the hard days come.
Arjuna stands between two armies, confused about which path to take. Krishna looks at him and says: And Krishna replied:
श्रेयान्स्वधर्मो विगुणः परधर्मात्स्वनुष्ठितात्, स्वभावनियतं कर्म कुर्वन्नाप्नोति किल्बिषम्.
In plain words: Better your own path, imperfectly walked, than someone else's done perfectly.

What you are living with is starting what is yours to build. This is easier said than done because the work will eventually feel messy and the results will not show up immediately. The truth underneath is that you do not carry a wrong for doing the work that fits you.
Let the brand be a sketch. Do your own work even when it is rough, and trust that the fire you feel is the right kind of heat.
What if the hard days are just the work showing you where it is rough?

depth.life: You are building a brand with no money and seven hours of phone time. The work feels like air. You want to keep this fire when the hard days come.
depth.points: The fire comes from doing what fits your own nature. That is your own duty. It is offered to the work itself, not to a result.
depth.practice: Write one line in your notebook about what the work felt like before you opened your phone today.
depth.question: What does the work feel like right now, before you check the numbers?
